ruleset.name: nitpicker-test-rules
ruleset.description: Nitpicker's PMD rules for test sources.

rule.name: FixedSleepInTest
rule.message: A fixed wait makes the test slow and flaky: a sleep or parkNanos outside a polling loop, after(ms) with a check that could pass sooner, or pollDelay(...).until(() -> true). Wait on the condition: a loop that checks it against a deadline (a sleep inside that loop is allowed), or verify(mock, timeout(1000)) for a mock. A timed wait, wait(ms) or join(ms), returns early but lets the test go on unchecked when the time runs out: assert the result of join(Duration) or of a latch await. A sleep in a mock answer, a thread body or a test fake that implements or extends a main class is allowed.

rule.name: FloatEqualityInTest
rule.message: Do not assert exact equality with a fractional floating-point literal: a computed 0.1 + 0.2 differs from 0.3 in the last bits, so the test fails on rounding noise or passes by luck. Give the comparison a tolerance: assertEquals(expected, actual, delta) in JUnit and TestNG, assertThat(actual).isCloseTo(expected, within(1e-9)) in AssertJ, or assertThat(actual, closeTo(expected, 1e-9)) in Hamcrest. The same goes for assertTrue(x == 0.1), assertThat(x == 0.1).isTrue() and Double.compare(x, 0.1) == 0. An integral literal such as 1.0 is exact and allowed.

rule.name: NegativeWaitInTest
rule.message: Do not prove that something does not happen by waiting out a delay: after(ms).never() and during(...) pass only after the full wait, so the test is slow and depends on the timing. Give the code a Clock or a scheduler the test controls, move it past the delay and assert at once.
